{"candidate_slot":0,"current_prompt":"Match a system inventory against CVE advisories; report only applicable CVE IDs.

Input: JSON with `system_profile` (product names + versions) and `advisories` (id, description, affected).

Output: exactly {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} with unique supplied IDs (empty array if none). No other text.

PRODUCT MATCHING:
1. Lowercase; treat hyphens, underscores, spaces, and slashes as equivalent separators.
2. Strip vendor/organization prefixes when the advisory name is vendor/product ("jetbrains/teamcity" = "teamcity"; "m-files/m-files_server" = "m-files-server"). Also strip a vendor prefix that starts the installed name.
3. Match ONLY when the ENTIRE normalized product name agrees after vendor stripping ("apache/superset" = "apache-superset" = "superset"). Ignore case.
4. Descriptions may restate the product name differently (Title Case, package-manager hyphens) — use them to confirm matches when naming style differs.
5. Do NOT match different products sharing a vendor ("jetbrains-hub" ≠ "jetbrains/teamcity"; "sap-solution-manager" ≠ "sap/content_server"). Partial token overlap is NOT a match. If no installed product matches, the CVE is NOT applicable even if the vendor appears in the inventory.
6. Multi-branch advisories (OR-separated): applicable if ANY branch matches an installed product AND that branch's version condition holds.

VERSION COMPARISON (mechanical, numeric, segment-wise — never approximate, never guess from magnitude of the gap):
1. Split on dots; compare segments AS INTEGERS left to right. Pad the shorter with zeros first: 3.6.1.0 == 3.6.1; 720.0 == 720; 1.0.0.0.0 == 1.0.0.0; 5.10.0.0 == 5.10.0.
2. At the first differing segment, decide by INTEGER order there and stop: 10 > 6; 100 > 45 (so 1.100 > 1.45); 115 > 2 (so 27.0.25.2 < 27.0.25.115 → AFFECTED by "< 27.0.25.115"); 22268 vs 22269 → 22269 > 22268 (so 2023.3.22269 is NOT < 2023.3.22268); 10 > 8 (so 10.10 is NOT < 10.8; 10.9 is NOT < 10.8); 757.1 > 757; 4.12.9 < 4.12.56860; 5.10 > 5.6; 2024.10 > 2024.2; 19.15.1 > 19.15.
3. Operators: "=" equality after zero-padding; "<" strict; "<=" inclusive (installed == bound IS affected); ">=" inclusive. Range ">= A and < B" means A <= installed < B.
4. Prose: "prior to X", "before X", "up to but excluding X", "versions prior to X are affected" → STRICT < X (installed == X is EXCLUDED). "up to and including X", "X and prior" → inclusive <= X. "version X" / "affecting version X" / "versions X and Y" → exact equality (after zero-padding) of X (or Y).
5. Date-like versions (20230913) and long builds are ordinary versions; compare numerically, segment by segment, exactly as stated.

DECISION PROCEDURE — for each advisory, do BOTH checks explicitly:
(a) PRODUCT: find installed products matching per rules 1-6. No match → skip (even if vendor or topic appears in inventory or description).
(b) VERSION: for each matched product, evaluate EVERY branch mechanically against the installed version. Compare segment-by-segment as integers with zero-padding; do NOT estimate, round, or reason about how "close" versions are.
   INCLUDE when the installed version satisfies a branch:
   - installed strictly BELOW a "<" bound — ANY version below the bound is affected, no matter how small the gap or how large the version numbers: 2023.1.16597.1 < 2024.3.47707 → AFFECTED; 2023.3.22269 < 2024.3.52635 → AFFECTED; 27.0.25.2 < 27.0.25.115 → AFFECTED; 9.0.17 < 9.0.18 → AFFECTED; 23.4.12528.2 < 23.11.13156.0 → AFFECTED; 1.21 < 1.22 → AFFECTED; 8.0.0.1 >= 8.0.0 and < 8.11.1 → AFFECTED.
   - installed AT or BELOW a "<=" bound: 19.15 <= 19.15 → AFFECTED; 8.6.5 <= 8.6.5 → AFFECTED.
   - installed EQUAL to an "=" bound after zero-padding: 720.0 == 720 → AFFECTED; 300.0 == 300 → AFFECTED; 1.1.0.0 == 1.1.0.0 → AFFECTED.
   EXCLUDE when the installed version fails the branch:
   - installed EQUAL to a strict "<" bound after padding: 2024.3.52635.1 vs "< 2024.3.52635"? First compare 2024.3.52635.1 vs 2024.3.52635.0 → last segment 1 > 0 → installed is ABOVE → EXCLUDED. Likewise 2024.3.47707.0 vs "< 2024.3.47707" → equal after padding → EXCLUDED; 3.6.1 vs "< 3.6.1" → EXCLUDED; 1.0.0.100 vs "< 1.0.0.100" → EXCLUDED; 5.10.0.0 vs "< 5.10.0" → EXCLUDED; 8.5.0.0 vs "< 8.5.0" → EXCLUDED; 23.11.13156.0 vs "< 23.11.13156.0" → EXCLUDED; 2024.12.0 vs "prior to 2024.12" → EXCLUDED; 9.1.6.0 vs "< 9.1.6" → EXCLUDED; 10.10 vs "< 10.8" → 10 > 8 → EXCLUDED.
   - installed ABOVE a strict bound at the first differing segment: 2.6.1 vs "= 2.6" → EXCLUDED; 2023.3.10 vs "< 2023.3.3" → 10 > 3 → EXCLUDED; 2024.2.x vs "< 2024.3.44799" → EXCLUDED; 11.1.1 vs "= 11.1 OR = 11.2" → EXCLUDED; 7.2.0.1 vs "= 7.2.0" and outside all ranges → EXCLUDED; 2023.3.22269 vs "< 2023.3.22268" → 22269 > 22268 → EXCLUDED; 1.100 vs "< 1.45" → 100 > 45 → EXCLUDED; 22.6.3.1 vs "< 22.6.3" → EXCLUDED; 3.7.10 vs ">= 3.0.0 and < 3.7.2" → 10 > 2 → EXCLUDED; 9.4.2.1 vs "<= 9.4.2" → EXCLUDED.
   - installed below a ">=" lower bound or above a "<=" upper bound → EXCLUDED (e.g., 7.17.2 vs ">= 8.4.0 and < 8.11.1" → 7 < 8 → EXCLUDED).
   NEVER include on product name alone without a satisfied version branch. NEVER drop a CVE whose version branch IS satisfied — including when the installed version is far below the bound (a lower version is always affected by a "<" bound), when inclusive bounds are exactly met, or when trailing zeros make versions equal (1.0.0.0.0 == 1.0.0.0 → AFFECTED).
(c) Report each applicable ID once.

REMINDERS:
- Alias-style naming differences (vendor/slash, hyphens, underscores, Title Case) never justify dropping a CVE — normalize and match.
- Trailing zeros: X.Y.Z.0 == X.Y.Z; X.Y.Z.1 > X.Y.Z.
- Decide equality vs exclusion by padding first: installed == strict bound → EXCLUDED; installed == inclusive or "=" bound → INCLUDED.
- Version segments are integers: compare 100 vs 45, 115 vs 2, 22269 vs 22268, 10 vs 8 numerically — never lexically, never as dates, never by "looks close".
- Evaluate each advisory independently; return only the JSON
